state.goal: Deliver a shared multidimensional radar experience while preserving distinct measures and attributed self/other perspectives, using existing scaffolding and explicit access contracts

artifacts.scope: Shared read-only radar experience over separate domain measures and perspectives

ux.reason: The owner selected one shared read-only experience with distinct measures and attributed perspectives. Existing journeys distinguish self-view from teacher viewing a learner; both must remain recognizable without merging their meanings.

screens.reason: Existing sources mention a student reflection radar and teacher classroom radar, while the chart renderer imports native React Native UI. Shared presentation must be evaluated against owned web/native UI boundaries and existing entry points.

state.reason: A read-only experience still needs separate active subject, measure, perspective and observation selection plus loading, empty, denied, unavailable and error states; existing source records do not define this combined state model.

errors.reason: The current student-potential API can return no row and can throw through its oRPC calls, while permission, source, and measure availability are contextual; the shared view needs explicit failure states and must not fabricate values.

feedback.reason: Users need to know which measure and whose perspective they are viewing, what date/source it reflects, and whether values are missing or unavailable; existing chart examples mainly label axes and numeric values.

motion.reason: Changing subject, measure, or perspective can change the polygon; transitions must not imply measured improvement or interpolate between unrelated constructs. Motion behavior is not specified in the supplied radar sources.

accessibility.reason: The present SVG chart labels axes visually but the supplied code does not establish an accessible textual equivalent for axis values, missingness, provenance, or perspective attribution.

data.reason: Existing domains define different axes, value ranges, subjects and histories. The shared view must preserve each measure's identity/version, units/range, per-axis missingness, provenance, timestamp and attributed perspective as provided, rather than inventing shared values.

api.reason: Student potential has an existing core API contract, but the owner requires current API admission rules and frozen legacy/direct-data paths to remain in force. Shared chart mechanics may use caller-supplied admitted data or clearly labelled synthetic examples.

database.reason: A legacy migration stores and overwrites one student-potential row per teacher/student/classroom, while personal growth and teacher-insight history use different event/state forms. The shared experience does not authorize a new persistence or history model.

dependencies.reason: Two existing chart implementations and separate graphics/UI packages are pinned by manifests and lockfile. A dependency or package change requires architecture review; the lockfile does not establish upstream compatibility or current releases.

security.reason: A self/other view depends on active identity, relationship, school/classroom scope, sharing state and private-data boundaries. The request does not grant cross-person visibility or editing authority.

offline.reason: The teacher-attunement flow declares an offline cached-roster path and local SQLite updates, but the new direction is read-only and does not establish an offline data source or freshness guarantee. Offline/unavailable must be shown distinctly.

reuse.reason: The owner requested evaluating platform-neutral core logic with owned web/native UI after architecture review. Existing geometry/UI code is reusable substrate only after its unit and rendering behavior are repaired and its platform boundary is resolved.

reuse: Evaluate a platform-neutral measure/geometry core and owned web/native components after Architecture review; this is the owner's proposed target, not an admitted production design.
Keep existing Self, Classroom and Profile records, entry points and behavior intact. The shared experience reads admitted values and does not replace or migrate their source records.

Before a new view uses RadarChart or SpiderChart, repair and verify the legacy geometry candidate: RadarSpiderChart.tsx computes each plotted vertex at the same full radius and does not scale by point.value or maxValue.
Synthetic examples must be visibly identified as synthetic and must not look like a real user's data.

Which per-measure metadata is available today for units/range, axis definitions/version, observation source, author/perspective, subject scope, timestamp, missingness, and confidence? No single current contract carries all of these.

What read authority and relationship context permits viewing another person's measure in each domain? This request does not answer it.
Can existing viewer contracts supply the read-only data without violating the API admission rules? No new direct database path or unadmitted capability is authorized.

artifacts.scope: Shared read-only radar experience for distinct domain measures

content.statement: Provide a shared read-only experience for viewing a person's existing multidimensional measures while preserving each measure's distinct definition and each perspective's attribution. This records the owner's clarification, 'Shared experience; distinct measures and perspectives' (research/coordination-study/lifecycle/radar/owner-request.md). It does not create a universal radar model or authorize new cross-person access.
acceptance: Render each selected existing measure using its own declared axes, value scale/units, measure identity/version and domain context. If those details are absent or unsupported, disclose that and do not substitute shared axes or a guessed range.

Keep self and other-person perspectives visibly attributed to the source/provenance supplied by the admitted caller. Show distinct perspectives separately; do not average, merge, rank, or infer that values are comparable.
Preserve missing, unavailable, denied and stale values as explicit states. Do not replace missing data with zero, silently omit it, or render an empty polygon as measured data.
Present loading, empty, source-unavailable, access-denied and recoverable-error states, with an accessible textual summary of axes, displayed values, units and missingness.

Operate read-only. Use caller-supplied results from an already admitted source or clearly labeled synthetic examples; do not add an endpoint, direct database path, write, edit, contribution, sharing grant, threshold alert or intervention.

Preserve the existing self-growth, teacher-student potential, teacher vitality and profile paths and their data. Integrate by an additive shared presentation seam only after Architecture identifies the appropriate platform-neutral core and owned web/native UI boundary.

Repair and verify the existing RadarChart/SpiderChart geometry before the new experience depends on it. The inspected RadarSpiderChart currently places each plotted vertex at the full radius without scaling by the value or maxValue; treat this as the first implementation repair candidate, not as evidence of a new business measure.
Synthetic fixtures are labeled synthetic throughout the view and are not presented as a real person's scores.
unresolved: The owner authorized shared presentation over distinct measures/perspectives. Measure definitions, score semantics, and cross-person visibility or editing authority remain unselected.
Existing domain endpoints and data contracts must be assessed for current API admission before live integration.
The first hosting routes/platforms and exact existing chart component are for Architecture and UX review.

The user selects one available domain measure and, where available, one separately attributed perspective.
The view receives axis definitions, scale/units and observation metadata from the caller.

A second measure or perspective is presented distinctly and never combined or compared by default.
Missing values remain visibly missing and are not treated as zero; no fabricated score or polygon is shown.
Empty, denied, stale, unavailable and error results have distinct truthful states; access-denied input reveals no values.
The view performs no writes and does not change the source record, existing route, sharing policy or domain-specific measure.
Synthetic examples are identified as synthetic and cannot be mistaken for a real person's record.

scenario

consumed.scope: Shared read-only radar experience over separate domain measures and perspectives

ux.reason: The owner selected one shared read-only experience with distinct measures and attributed perspectives. Existing journeys distinguish self-view from teacher viewing a learner; both must remain recognizable without merging their meanings.

screens.reason: Existing sources mention a student reflection radar and teacher classroom radar, while the chart renderer imports native React Native UI. Shared presentation must be evaluated against owned web/native UI boundaries and existing entry points.

state.reason: A read-only experience still needs separate active subject, measure, perspective and observation selection plus loading, empty, denied, unavailable and error states; existing source records do not define this combined state model.

errors.reason: The current student-potential API can return no row and can throw through its oRPC calls, while permission, source, and measure availability are contextual; the shared view needs explicit failure states and must not fabricate values.

feedback.reason: Users need to know which measure and whose perspective they are viewing, what date/source it reflects, and whether values are missing or unavailable; existing chart examples mainly label axes and numeric values.

motion.reason: Changing subject, measure, or perspective can change the polygon; transitions must not imply measured improvement or interpolate between unrelated constructs. Motion behavior is not specified in the supplied radar sources.

accessibility.reason: The present SVG chart labels axes visually but the supplied code does not establish an accessible textual equivalent for axis values, missingness, provenance, or perspective attribution.

data.reason: Existing domains define different axes, value ranges, subjects and histories. The shared view must preserve each measure's identity/version, units/range, per-axis missingness, provenance, timestamp and attributed perspective as provided, rather than inventing shared values.

api.reason: Student potential has an existing core API contract, but the owner requires current API admission rules and frozen legacy/direct-data paths to remain in force. Shared chart mechanics may use caller-supplied admitted data or clearly labelled synthetic examples.

database.reason: A legacy migration stores and overwrites one student-potential row per teacher/student/classroom, while personal growth and teacher-insight history use different event/state forms. The shared experience does not authorize a new persistence or history model.

dependencies.reason: Two existing chart implementations and separate graphics/UI packages are pinned by manifests and lockfile. A dependency or package change requires architecture review; the lockfile does not establish upstream compatibility or current releases.

security.reason: A self/other view depends on active identity, relationship, school/classroom scope, sharing state and private-data boundaries. The request does not grant cross-person visibility or editing authority.

offline.reason: The teacher-attunement flow declares an offline cached-roster path and local SQLite updates, but the new direction is read-only and does not establish an offline data source or freshness guarantee. Offline/unavailable must be shown distinctly.

reuse.reason: The owner requested evaluating platform-neutral core logic with owned web/native UI after architecture review. Existing geometry/UI code is reusable substrate only after its unit and rendering behavior are repaired and its platform boundary is resolved.
